topic: Ocean with the most tsunamis: the Pacific — roughly 70 % of recorded tsunamis (NOAA NCEI/WDS Global Historical Tsunami Database; ITIC), generated along the Pacific Ring of Fire subduction zones; the deadliest tsunami on record was the 26 December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (~230,000 deaths, 14 countries); Japan records the most tsunamis of any country and gave the world the word (tsu = harbour, nami = wave); World Tsunami Awareness Day, 5 November, designated by the UN General Assembly in 2015
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Tsunamis are an Indian Ocean problem because of 2004.
myths.reality: About 7 in 10 recorded tsunamis occur in the Pacific; the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was the deadliest, not the typical one.

britannica_tsunami.title: Tsunami

jma_2011.title: 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami

claims.text: About 70 % of recorded tsunamis occur in the Pacific Ocean, generated along the Ring of Fire.
vo: which ocean produces the most tsunamis
the pacific. about 7 in 10 tsunamis on record start there, along the ring of quakes around its rim

claims.text: The deadliest tsunami on record was the 26 December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, which killed around 230,000 people.
vo: the deadliest, though, came from the indian ocean in 2004, and killed around 230,000 people

claims.text: Japan records more tsunamis than any other country and gave the world the word tsunami, meaning harbour wave.
vo: japan is hit more often than anywhere; its own word, harbour wave, is what the world uses

claims.text: World Tsunami Awareness Day is 5 November; the core safety message is to move to high ground after a strong or long earthquake near the coast.
vo: the 5th of november is world tsunami awareness day. the lesson: feel a long quake, head for high ground
